source: W3C ARIA APG, Slider pattern — Keyboard Interaction. https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/slider/
note: Framework-neutral cases. A backend passes this file or it has not implemented the primitive. `apg` records how the specification treats each case: `unmarked` is stated plainly, `optional` is offered as a choice, `not-addressed` is OURS and says so. Every pointer case is `not-addressed`, because the APG specifies a slider's KEYBOARD and says nothing at all about pointer behaviour — that part of a slider is inherently visual and the specification declines to describe it.

cases.quote: Right Arrow: Increase the value of the slider by one step.
Up Arrow: Increase the value of the slider by one step.
Left Arrow: Decrease the value of the slider by one step.
Down Arrow: Decrease the value of the slider by one step.
The APG lists all four arrows for a slider without qualifying them by orientation, which is the opposite of the rule it gives a tab list. A horizontal slider still answers Up and Down.
Home: Set the slider to the first allowed value in its range.
End: Set the slider to the last allowed value in its range.
Page Up (Optional): Increase the value of the slider by an amount larger than the step change made by Up Arrow.
Page Down (Optional): Decrease the value of the slider by an amount larger than the step change made by Down Arrow.
Page Up and Page Down are marked Optional, so a contract that declares no jump size has not asked for them, and the key must reach the page instead of being swallowed.
A slider does not wrap. Its range has ends, unlike a collection of members where the last is adjacent to the first.
A slider does not wrap.
Never reports a value outside its range.
Increase the value of the slider by one step — the step is the contract's, not the platform's.
Set the slider to the last ALLOWED value in its range. With a step of 30 counted from 0, the maximum of 100 is not an allowed value and 90 is.
Steps are counted from the minimum, not from zero.
OURS. Repeated floating-point addition drifts, and a slider reporting 0.7999999999999999 through aria-valuenow is announced as that number.
OURS. A controlled value is the consumer's to set and may be off-step; the contract says the slider never reports a value between steps.
OURS. Clamp first, then step, so one press brings a wild controlled value back inside the range rather than moving it further out.
OURS, and the same rule the navigation primitive follows: consuming a key the pattern does not define breaks whatever else would have used it.
A slider is a single Tab stop; Tab must leave it.
OURS. The APG specifies no pointer behaviour for a slider at all.
OURS.
OURS. Snapping to the NEAREST step, not to the one below it: a thumb dragged to 0.46 of a ten-step range is closer to 50 than to 40 and should give 50.
OURS.
OURS. A pointer keeps sending coordinates after it leaves the track, and the value must not follow it out of range.
OURS.
OURS. The fill's length and the thumb's offset ARE the value, and a backend needs exactly one number to draw both.
OURS. A minimum equal to its maximum is a legal contract, and the obvious arithmetic divides by zero.
